title.value: Predicting Tactical Solutions to Operational Planning Problems under Imperfect Information
title.justification: The title reflects the content of the paper which focuses on predicting tactical solutions in operational planning using machine learning and operations research.
title.quote: This paper offers a methodological contribution at the intersection of machine learning and operations research. Namely, we propose a methodology to quickly predict expected tactical descriptions of operational solutions (TDOSs).

extractions.description: This paper integrates machine learning and operations research to develop a high-speed predictive methodology for tactical solutions in two-stage stochastic programming. It demonstrates this through an application in rail transportation load planning, predicting tactical descriptions of operational solutions under imperfect information.

primary_category.justification: The paper is related to transportation, which is a crucial sector for climate change mitigation, as improvements in transportation planning can reduce emissions by optimizing operations.
primary_category.quote: Results on our motivating application on load planning for rail transportation show that deep learning models produce accurate predictions in very short computing time.

secondary_categories.justification: The paper does not directly address other predefined eco-responsible categories beyond the application in transportation planning.
secondary_categories.quote: Our methodology could also be applied in the context of the general sequential booking problem to the prediction of the expected value achieved in the operational loading problem.

primary_sub_category.justification: The focus of the paper is on improving rail transportation load planning through predictive modeling, optimizing capacity usage, and enhancing the decision-making process, which directly aligns with the transportation sub-category.
primary_sub_category.quote: We consider a myopic, two-stage booking control problem pertaining to cargo capacity management... an NP-hard operational multidimensional bin packing problem must be solved.

secondary_sub_categories.justification: The paper's application is specific to transportation and does not extend to other sub-categories.
secondary_sub_categories.quote: Our predictions stem from supervised ML. They account for the stochasticity in the second stage problem and can approximate its expected solution at a higher online speed.

applications.justification: The primary application discussed in the paper is rail transportation load planning and the prediction of tactical solutions to improve operational efficiency.
applications.quote: To illustrate the methodology, we specialize the two-stage booking problem to reflect the booking decisions made about the shipment of intermodal containers by rail.

new_primary_category.justification: The categories provided cover the scope of the paper, particularly focusing on transportation within climate change mitigation.
new_primary_category.quote: In addition, the advance information embodied in the expected TDOS can be used to plan the railcar and container layouts in the terminal.

new_primary_sub_category.justification: The sub-categories provided sufficiently cover the domain of the paper, specifically under transportation.
new_primary_sub_category.quote: The idea underlying the proposed methodology is simple and attractive: predict the expected TDOS, conditionally on first stage variables, using supervised ML.
